correctness.rationale: Marked Ewens cycle-count factorial moments reduce exactly to a product F_n(m) of n-dependent factors; those factors strictly increase/decrease with marked length according as theta<1 or >1. Covariance and size-exclusion signs follow. Fixed-length logarithmic expansion yields limit theta^2(1-theta). Theta=2 telescopes; comparing Cov(C_1,C_2) and Cov(C_1,C_3) gives an exact rational factor proportional to (theta-1)(theta-2) with positive denominator. Thus theta=1,2 are necessary and sufficient for all-admissible-pair equicovariance when n>=4. The included rational verifier passed 1,165 exact finite assertions. Infinite quantified claims depend on the proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The Ewens parameter governs a canonical random-permutation law. A universal strict phase transition for mixed factorial moment dependence is a motivated finite-sample structural classification, not an isolated arithmetic example; the fixed-length covariance is unexpectedly independent of cycle lengths to leading order, and only one positive nontrivial parameter theta=2 gives exactly equal off-diagonal covariances for every n>=4 and admissible length pair. This is a meaningful natural exact parameter rigidity statement even though it follows from classical distributional ingredients.
